title: perf: decode string bodies once instead of per chunk
prompt:
For string parsers, including the default JSON parser, `rawBody` called `setEncoding('utf8')`. On every request that meant:

- a new StringDecoder,
- decoding each chunk separately,
- building the body with `body += chunk`,
- running `Buffer.byteLength()` over every decoded chunk just to enforce `bodyLimit`.

On a JSON POST profile this came to about 6% of busy CPU, more than routing, validation and hooks combined.

This PR always reads raw Buffers and counts bytes with `chunk.length`. String bodies are decoded once at the end, with no copy when the body arrived in a single chunk. Buffer parsers still receive a `Buffer.concat` copy, so they never get a view over the shared socket read buffer. String chunks from a custom `preParsing` stream are converted with `Buffer.from`.

### Bug fix

The limit and `Content-Length` checks used to count bytes after decoding. An invalid UTF-8 byte decodes to U+FFFD, which is 3 bytes when counted again. So a body with the correct `Content-Length` was rejected with `FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH`. Both checks now count the bytes actually received.

### Benchmarks

`autocannon -d 8`, POST `application/json`, `logger: false`. Five rounds, alternating `main` and this branch; figures are median req/s.

| Body | Settings | main | PR | Change | Rounds PR won |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `{"hello":"world"}` (18 B) | `-c 50 -p 10` | 141,572 | 147,728 | **+4.3%** | 4/5 |
| JSON object, 888 B | `-c 100 -p 10` | 97,392 | 100,736 | **+3.4%** | 4/5 |
| JSON with multi-byte characters, 157 KB | `-c 50 -p 1` | 1,841 | 2,263 | **+22.9%** | 5/5 |

Apple M5 Pro, Node v24.18.0.
